mechanism.error: ValueError: require-resolver profile selector order drift
sequence: resume() calls configure_shared() and performs the SHA-fixed aggregate closure
main(resume) then calls check() in the same Python process
check() calls configure_shared() a second time
PRODUCT.configure() reaches the one-shot require-resolver profile selector again
mechanism.second_selector_state: .rodata.vm_callprim already = 166 bytes while the one-shot selector requires its 164-byte predecessor
mechanism.cause: The resume wrapper repeats a deliberately one-shot global product configuration before readback. This is the same lifecycle class already caught by the Link-92 startup gate; the generated aggregate bytes are not implicated.
mechanism.classification: Post-write readback-checker lifecycle error, not product, dependency closure, media bytes, compiler, linker, capacity, device or release.

disposition.recommendation: Repair only the wrapper/readback lifecycle: one product configuration per process, with a loud mutation that reintroduces same-process double configuration. Then perform a resume-safe readback replay against the four SHA-fixed aggregate outputs without regenerating product, shared media, either library D81 or any aggregate manifest. Green may promote the persisted aggregate receipt to the two-variant media authority and open Phase D.

claim_limit: The semantic resolver contract and aggregate writes are complete, but their post-write readback did not start. The persisted aggregate receipt is frozen output, not yet acceptance authority. There is no media-closed contract state, Phase D, Halt or release claim.
